'''John D. Branon''', sometimes known simply as '''John "D"''', was a young [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A member of the [[Tierfon Yellow Aces/Legends|Tierfon Yellow Aces]], Branon was a friend of fellow pilot [[Jek Tono Porkins/Legends|Jek Porkins]], who attested to his bravery and recommended him as a replacement for the fallen [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] pilot [[Cesi Eirriss]].<ref name="TEGW" />

In [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he participated in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] under the callsign [[Red Four/Legends|Red Four]]. Flying a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]], Branon was shot down by [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] during the assault on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], among the first pilots who were killed. He and [[Theron Nett/Legends|Theron Nett]] were the only Rebels known to die at the hands of [[TIE pilot]]s during the battle, as the rest of the known X- and [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wings]] that fell during the battle were destroyed by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] or gunned down by turbolaser fire.<ref name="TCSWE" />

==Behind the scenes==
John D. was portrayed by [[Jack Klaff]] in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']]. He was presumably named after [[John Dykstra]].<ref name="Insider95">{{InsiderCite|95|Pirates of the Boards|Pirates of the Boards, Part 4}}</ref>

Though the film credits list Jack Klaff as the actor portraying John D, the [[Special Edition Limited|Customizable Card Game]] names Jack Klaff's character Lt. [[Nozzo Naytaan/Legends|Naytaan]]. The CCG creators made an error in naming him Naytaan. According to [[Leland Chee]], Naytaan and John D. are two different pilots.<ref>{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=1695#17083464|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2008-01-10|time=3:09 PM}}</ref>

According to Klaff, he was recorded with additional dialogue which was subsequently cut&mdash;noting that he had his first TIE fighter kill right before being shot down.<ref name="Insider32">{{InsiderCite|32|Rebel Pilot Reunion}}</ref>

John D. has been known as "[[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Fake Wedge]]" among much of the Star Wars community, because of the belief that Jack Klaff played the character of Wedge in the Rebel briefing room scene (a character played by [[Denis Lawson]] in every other scene). [[Pablo Hidalgo]] has since revealed that "Fake Wedge" was not actually portrayed by Klaff, but rather by actor [[Colin Higgins]].<ref name="pablog">{{Blog|pablog|37|The Hunt for the Fake Wedge}}</ref>

Branon's helmet prop from the films — or possibly one of a matching design — was later worn by [[Tenk Lenso]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|Star Wars: Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]<ref name="MP Documentary">''[[The Making of "The Empire Strikes Back"]]''</ref> and [[Ace Merrick]] in the video game [[Star Wars: Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire|''Rebel Assault II: The Hidden Empire'']].<ref name="RAII video">{{LucasArts|url=products/rebel2/reb_vid.htm|text=''Rebel Assault II'' - Live Action Video}}</ref>
